Two offices sit at 99 Courthouse Hill in Dahlonega, a few suite numbers apart. One handles value and exemptions. The other handles billing and collection.

You can search, view and pay property tax on the commissioner's website. Bills go to homeowners only and never to lenders, so if your taxes are escrowed, send a copy to your mortgage company.

sections.h2: Homes and buyers in Lumpkin County
sections.html:
Dahlonega is the county seat. Lumpkin County has an estimated 36,178 residents as of mid-2025, up 8.0% from 33,486 in 2020, spread over about 283 square miles of land. It has 14,302 housing units, and owners occupy 76.3% of homes. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $307,900, and builders pulled 270 permits in 2025.

About 20.6% of residents are past 65. That matters at tax time, because several exemptions in the county's flyer begin at 62 or 65.

sections.h2: What Lumpkin County bills and what lateness costs
sections.html:
December 1 is the due date for houses, land and business equipment. It was December 20 until the county commissioners signed a resolution in December 2009 moving it up.

  • After the due date, a 5% penalty arrives at the 120 day mark and returns every 120 days until the total reaches 20%.
  • Past 90 days late, a tax fifa (lien) can go on record at the courthouse.
  • Levy on the property is possible, though the commissioner calls it a last resort.
  • Credit bureaus can see the lien, and the tax office has no control over how they use it.

Mobile homes run on their own calendar, so an owner of one should phone 706-864-2666 for that date. A location permit is issued only after the current year's mobile home tax has been paid in full.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Lumpkin County value
sections.html:
Three routes exist, and each begins with a written appeal filed within 45 days of the notice date. Grounds include whether the property is taxable, its value, uniformity, or a refused exemption.

  • Board of Equalization: the assessors look first and may revise the value in a new notice, which the owner has 30 days to contest. Otherwise it goes automatically to a hearing, and Superior Court is the next stop.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser takes value or uniformity disputes on non-homestead real property above $500,000, or on certain wireless property above that same level.
  • Arbitration: the owner submits a certified appraisal, and the assessors either accept it or certify the appeal to the Clerk of Superior Court for arbitration.

The state provides a uniform appeal form, and you name your chosen route in that first written filing. Unsure which fits your case? Call the assessors at 706-864-2433 before filing.

Before you file, gather a few recent sales of similar homes nearby and note anything wrong in the parcel record, such as square footage or a feature the house does not have. Specific evidence gives the board something to act on.

The standard state homestead exemption subtracts $2,000 from assessed value, set by law at 40% of market value. You qualify by owning the home and living in it on January 1. Applications can go in all year, but one received after April 1 starts with the following year. Owners who reach 62 can apply for an additional exemption.

The county's tax information flyer, last dated 2021, also describes local and special programs. Ask the assessors for the current amounts before you rely on any of these.

  • School tax break for owners 62 and over whose federal adjusted gross income is at most $20,000: $30,000 off assessed value.
  • Owners 65 and up, or permanently disabled: as much as $120,000 off for school tax and $60,000 off for county tax, covering the home and at most 5 adjoining acres.
  • Agricultural preferential assessment: qualifying land is assessed at 30% instead of the usual 40%, under a 10-year covenant that carries penalties if broken.
  • Forest land conservation use: 200 acres or more in total, with parcels of 100 acres or more inside the county.
  • Tax deferral: owners 62 or older with household income under $15,000 can postpone the tax, which is different from an exemption.

A conservation use application (PT-283A) needs a notary's signature and must go in by April 1 with a $25.00 recording fee, because the original is recorded at the courthouse. A senior application should enclose a state ID showing birth date and address, and a disabled veteran application needs the VA letter showing a 100% combined rating.

County appraisers make field inspections across Lumpkin County under state law. They carry identification, drive marked vehicles, measure exteriors, take photographs and note improvements. Entering a home is generally unnecessary, and you do not need to be present. Commercial and industrial appraisals are handled for the board by McCormick Solutions, a division of LMC, Inc, whose staff wear county-issued badges you can ask to see.

Forms can be downloaded from the state revenue department's site and mailed in, and the assessors ask for a USPS postmark no later than April 1. They include the state homestead form, the business personal property return (PT-50P), the freeport application (PT-50F), the marine (PT-50M) and airplane (PT-50A) returns, and PT-50R, the taxpayer return of value used to ask for a review.

State law puts the full year on whoever owned the parcel January 1, and a mid-year sale earns no refund.

  1. Before listing, phone the commissioner at 706-864-2666 and ask what is still owed on the parcel, interest or lien included.
  2. Hand that number to the closing attorney.
  3. Clear any unpaid fifa before closing.
  4. Send any bill that reaches you after closing to the buyer.

An inherited, tax-delinquent or rented house goes through the same sequence. Ask the assessors early whether a senior exemption or deferral is attached to the account, since it can change what is owed at the closing table. A cash buyer will still expect the lien cleared.

Bring your closing statement, your most recent bill and the parcel number when you visit the commissioner's office. If the tax was prorated between you and the buyer, the signed statement shows who took on the bill. Keep the receipt for any payment you make, since the closing attorney will ask for proof that the account is current.

faqs.q: When is Lumpkin County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 1 for houses, land and business equipment. Before a December 2009 resolution by the county commissioners, the usual date had been December 20.

faqs.q: How long is the Lumpkin County dispute window?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice date. Send a written filing to the assessors at 99 Courthouse Hill, Suite C, and say which route you pick.

faqs.q: Does Lumpkin County send my bill to my mortgage company?
faqs.a: No. Bills go to the homeowner, never the lender, so an owner with an escrow account should send a copy to the mortgage company.

faqs.q: When must a Lumpkin County homestead application arrive?
faqs.a: The assessors need it by April 1 for it to count this tax year. A later one starts with the following year.

faqs.q: Which office should a Lumpkin County seller call first?
faqs.a: Start with the commissioner at 706-864-2666 to learn what is owed. Use the assessors at 706-864-2433 for value or exemption questions.
